what: Krystal Biotech makes Vyjuvek, a gene therapy applied as a gel to the wounds of people with dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, a genetic condition in which the skin blisters and tears at the slightest touch.
customers: Dermatologists and specialist centres treating a rare inherited skin disease, paid for by insurers.
money: the topical gene therapy for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
early-stage programmes in respiratory, oncology and ophthalmology
moat: The first and only approved topical gene therapy, delivered repeatedly rather than once, and manufactured in its own facility for a disease with no alternative treatment.
risks: 43 times earnings and 20 times sales: a high price for a single-product company
The patient population is small, so growth depends on launching in new countries
Any manufacturing or supply problem would stop all revenue at once
opportunities: Revenue grew from $51M to $389M in two years and is $470M over the last twelve months
A 52.6% net margin and $828M of cash against $9M of debt
The same delivery platform is being tested in respiratory and eye diseases, which are far larger markets
watch: European and Japanese launch progress, and readouts from the pipeline programmes.
